paragraphs.paragraph: The Peaceful Announcement and Judah’s Restoration
paragraphs.title: The Peaceful Announcement and Judah’s Restoration

easy.explanation: Nahum 1:15 says, “Behold upon the mountains the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace.”
easy.q: What does the messenger proclaim upon the mountains?

answers: Celebrate her feasts and perform her vows
easy.explanation: The surrounding prophecy calls Judah to rejoice because the wicked enemy will no longer pass through the land.
easy.q: What is Judah told to do?

answers: He will be completely cut off
easy.explanation: The passage declares that the enemy will be cut off and will no longer pass through Judah.
easy.q: What will happen to the wicked enemy?

answers: Peace allows Judah to celebrate safely
medium.explanation: The end of the enemy’s oppression provides the reason for Judah to celebrate and fulfill her vows.
medium.q: What is the connection between the announcement of peace and Judah’s celebration?

answers: Watch the way, strengthen his loins, and fortify his power
medium.explanation: Nahum 2:1 says, “keep the munition, watch the way, make thy loins strong, fortify thy power mightily.”
medium.q: What is the commander told to do before the attack?

answers: The enemies stripped them of their strength and possessions
The people held a joyful feast
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the enemies’ destruction and removal of Jacob’s wealth and strength.
medium.q: What does “the emptiers have emptied them out” mean?

answers: God’s people should keep their commitments after receiving salvation
challenge.explanation: The prophecy connects deliverance with faithful worship and the fulfillment of vows.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the call to fulfill vows after deliverance?

answers: The enemies emptied and damaged Jacob, so God restores his excellency
The enemies had no effect on Jacob
challenge.explanation: The enemies “emptied them out” and “marred their vine branches,” yet the LORD promises the restoration of Jacob’s excellency.
challenge.q: How does the restoration of Jacob relate to the actions of his enemies?

answers: A change from enemy oppression to peace and restoration
A change from celebration to permanent war
A change from peace to Judah’s exile
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the enemy’s oppression to peace, celebration, and the restoration of God’s people.
challenge.q: What major change is described in this passage?

paragraphs.idea: The Peaceful Announcement and Judah’s Restoration

paragraphs.paragraph: Battle Preparations and the Charge of the Chariots
paragraphs.title: Battle Preparations and the Charge of the Chariots

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:3 says, “The shield of his mighty men is made red.”
easy.q: What color is the shield of the mighty men?

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:4 says, “The chariots shall rage in the streets.”
The chariots “shall seem like torches” and “shall run like the lightnings.”
easy.q: What are the chariots compared to?

answers: They rage through the streets and run like lightning
They move slowly across a field
medium.explanation: Their movement through the streets and comparison with lightning emphasize their speed.
medium.q: What creates the sense of speed in the description of the chariots?

answers: Reach the wall and prepare the defense
medium.explanation: Nahum 2:5 says they “make haste to the wall thereof, and the defence shall be prepared.”
medium.q: What do the leaders attempt to do during the attack?

answers: The red clothing of the valiant men
medium.explanation: The verse says, “The valiant men are in scarlet,” describing their appearance in battle.

answers: The battle is dangerous, swift, and powerful
The city is enjoying a time of peace
challenge.explanation: These vivid images emphasize the force, speed, and terrifying appearance of the attack.
challenge.q: What does the combination of red shields, flaming torches, and lightning suggest?

answers: It creates the feeling of a sudden, overwhelming assault
It shows that the soldiers are resting
challenge.explanation: Words such as “rage,” “justle,” “run,” and “make haste” create an impression of chaotic military action.
challenge.q: Why does the repeated description of movement strengthen the battle scene?

answers: The defense of the city versus the power of the assault
challenge.explanation: The defenders hurry to prepare the wall, while the attacking chariots advance with overwhelming force.
challenge.q: What is the central tension in the passage?

paragraphs.idea: Battle Preparations and the Charge of the Chariots

paragraphs.paragraph: The Breach, Fall, and Plunder of the City
paragraphs.title: The Breach, Fall, and Plunder of the City

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:6 says, “The gates of the rivers shall be opened.”
easy.q: What is opened at the beginning of the city’s fall?

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:8 says, “yet they shall flee away.”
easy.q: What happens to the people of the city?

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:9 commands, “Take ye the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold.”
easy.q: What is done with the silver and gold?

answers: It contributes to the city’s destruction
It allows the city to celebrate
medium.explanation: The opening of the gates is presented with the dissolving of the palace and the collapse of the city.
medium.q: How does the opening of the river gates relate to the city’s fall?

medium.explanation: These words portray Nineveh as devastated and emptied of its former glory.
medium.q: What does “empty, and void, and waste” describe?

answers: The plunder ends the war peacefully
Fear prevents any damage to the city
medium.explanation: The stolen wealth and the melting hearts, trembling knees, and darkened faces all show Nineveh’s defeat.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the plundered treasures and the people’s fear?

answers: The city’s humiliation and loss of control
challenge.explanation: Huzzab and her maids being led away captive represents the defeat and humiliation of Nineveh.
challenge.q: What does the leading away of Huzzab and her maids symbolize?

answers: The wealth is taken, leaving the city ruined
It proves that the city was never wealthy
It describes the success of the city’s defense
challenge.explanation: Although Nineveh possesses abundant treasure, the invaders take it and leave the city empty and waste.
challenge.q: Why is the contrast between abundant treasures and emptiness significant?

answers: Plunder, then attack, then the opening of the rivers
The city’s breach, flight, plunder, and overwhelming fear
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the city’s breach and collapse to the flight of its people, the taking of its treasures, and widespread terror.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the passage?

paragraphs.idea: The Breach, Fall, and Plunder of the City

paragraphs.paragraph: Nineveh as a Lions’ Den and Its Judgment
paragraphs.title: Nineveh as a Lions’ Den and Its Judgment

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:11 asks, “Where is the dwelling of the lions?” referring to Nineveh’s former power.

answers: They tore it and stored it in their dens
They brought it to a feast
easy.explanation: The lion “filled his holes with prey, and his dens with ravin.”
easy.q: What did the lions do with their prey?

easy.explanation: Nahum 2:13 says, “I will burn her chariots in the smoke.”
easy.q: What does the LORD promise to do to Nineveh’s chariots?

answers: Its rulers preyed on others and gathered spoil
The city was a place of peace
medium.explanation: The lions tear, strangle, and store prey, representing Nineveh’s violent gathering of wealth and power.
medium.q: What does comparing Nineveh to a lions’ den suggest?

medium.explanation: The lion fills its den with prey, meaning what it has captured or taken from others.
medium.q: What does “prey” mean in this context?

answers: Burning the chariots, destroying the young lions, and cutting off the prey
medium.explanation: The LORD promises to burn the chariots, let the sword devour the young lions, and cut off the prey and messengers.
medium.q: What judgments are mentioned in the LORD’s declaration?

answers: The punishment fits a city that preyed on others and stored up spoil
The imagery has no connection to the judgment
The imagery proves that Nineveh will be rescued
challenge.explanation: Nineveh is judged as a predatory power, and its chariots, rulers, spoil, and messengers are removed.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the lion imagery and Nineveh’s judgment?

answers: The continued rule of Nineveh’s messengers
The end of Nineveh’s voice and influence
The return of the chariots to the city
challenge.explanation: The silencing of the messengers signifies the end of Nineveh’s authority and communication.
challenge.q: What does the statement that the voice of the messengers will no longer be heard emphasize?

answers: From a powerful predator to a condemned power facing destruction
From a weak creature to a victorious ruler
From a protector of the city to a messenger of peace
challenge.explanation: The lion first appears strong, fearless, and rich in prey, but the passage ends with the LORD declaring its destruction.
challenge.q: How does the image of the lion change throughout the passage?

paragraphs.idea: Nineveh as a Lions’ Den and Its Judgment
